definition: As of the early 2000s, several speech recognition (SR) software packages exist for Linux.
details: Some of them are free and open-source software and others are proprietary software. Speech recognition usually refers to software that attempts to distinguish thousands of words in a human language. Voice control may refer to software used for communicating operational commands to a computer.

explainer.lead: A category of speech recognition packages available for Linux since the early 2000s, spanning free and open-source software and proprietary software. It matters to teams running speech pipelines on Linux who need to know both licence-bearing and commercial options exist.

tiers.eli5: Just like there are many apps for your phone that listen to you and write down what you say, there are versions of that kind of program built to run on the Linux operating system.
tiers.practitioner: On Linux, engineers choose between free and open-source packages and proprietary ones depending on licence constraints. Note the distinction in the category between true speech recognition, which attempts to distinguish thousands of words, and voice control, which maps spoken commands to computer operations.
tiers.paperLevel: No single formal definition: the category covers SR software for Linux, free and open-source or proprietary, with speech recognition typically aiming to distinguish thousands of words in a human language while voice control sends operational commands to a computer.

explainer.example: A developer building a voice-controlled desktop tool on Linux picks a voice control package, while a team building dictation picks a speech recognition package that handles thousands of words.
